obligations.condition: A fresh pending credential completes the phone second factor while the account is enabled; its identity is confirmed by claims and a derived lookup.

The account is disabled through privileged accounts:update and read back; the pending credential obtained before the disable is presented to mfaSignIn:start. Accepted and refused are both valid observations; USER_DISABLED is not pinned as the answer.
If the disabled start returned a session, that session is finalized; skipped otherwise. Either outcome is recorded.
The account is re-enabled and read back; the same pending credential is presented to mfaSignIn:start, showing whether the disabled attempt consumed it.
If the re-enabled start returned a session, it is finalized and the identity confirmed.
A fresh sign-in completes the second factor after the run, bounding it against a broken account.

limitations: URLs were read during design; no new frozen full-body source snapshot or completed page-review claim is made by this mapping.

The sources define the operations; none states whether mfaSignIn:start on a disabled account is refused or accepted, or at which step the disabled state is enforced. The observation, not the sources, answers that for the recorded conditions.
One account, one SMS session, phone MFA with a test phone number, no tenant, no blocking function, one run. The pending credential is obtained before the disable.

The oracle project's MFA, phone sign-in and SMS region configuration were changed for the run and restored; the restore readback and whole-configuration digest comparison are part of the receipt, not a claim about production defaults.
No execution approval, independent signature verification, SDK, Rules or expiry claim follows from this mapping.
